name: Portugal
headline: Portugal: +1.9% growth in 2025, 2.2% inflation, debt 90% of GDP
sections: Portugal is a $346 billion economy (2025), the world's 47th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.9% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $53K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 11.3% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.2% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.0% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 20.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 90% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 134% in 2020. The general government balance is +0.7% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +1.2% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 86% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 72% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.4 years (2024). Population: 10.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
